notes: These exercise the semantic half only — the five judgement checks in SKILL.md. The mechanical half is covered by the 235-test suite in tool/tests. Each fixture is a local clone of a real repository, pinned so the ground truth is stable. An assertion that every model passes teaches nothing, so each eval names the failure mode it is discriminating against.

evals.name: feature-map-honesty
evals.prompt: Run project-standard against this repo and tell me whether docs/FEATURE_MAP.md is honest about what the code does today.
evals.fixture: isitgood-auction pinned at d4570c59, the parent of 8e3edc3a ("docs(feature-map): correct four claims that were not true of the code"). That commit touches only the document, so the code was already right and the doc was wrong — the corrections it makes are the ground truth.
evals.expected_output: Names the false claims in FEATURE_MAP.md, each cited against the source that contradicts it.
evals.failure_mode: Accepting a clean mechanical `check` run as sufficient and never opening the source. This is semantic check 2, the one SKILL.md calls the highest hit rate; a model that stops at the CLI has skipped the half the skill exists for. A fabricated finding fails equally.
expectations: Runs the mechanical check first, then reads source files rather than stopping at the CLI output
Flags the confidence-scoring row: it claims the rating derives partly from price availability, but the scoring function reads no comp or price inputs
Flags the authenticity row: the vision read is marked unconditionally live when it executes but has never been scored against a listing that should fail
Cites specific document lines against specific source lines
Reports no claim as false that is in fact true of the code

evals.name: trust-stamp-plausibility
evals.prompt: Is this repo's documentation trustworthy right now? Check docs/PROJECT_MAP.md specifically.
evals.fixture: isitgood-auction at HEAD. docs/PROJECT_MAP.md is stamped `As of: v0.13.2`; docs/FEATURE_MAP.md is stamped `As of: v0.16.0`; the repo's latest tag is v0.16.2. Two stamps in one repo, several releases apart.
evals.expected_output: Flags the PROJECT_MAP stamp as stale against the repo's actual version, and separately assesses whether the body is still accurate.
evals.failure_mode: Two opposite errors. Treating the presence of a stamp as proof of freshness — conflating stamped with current — or condemning the whole document as wrong without checking whether its content still holds. Staleness and inaccuracy are independent findings.
expectations: Notices the stamp lags the repo's current version and flags it as stale or unverified
Establishes the repo's actual version from tags rather than assuming
Notices that FEATURE_MAP.md in the same repo carries a much fresher stamp
Treats stamp staleness and body accuracy as two separate findings rather than inferring one from the other

evals.name: override-genuineness
evals.prompt: Check whether this repo's project-standard contract overrides are legitimate or dodging something.
evals.fixture: llm-preflight at HEAD. AGENTS.md declares next-steps, release-flow and prds as `local` with a stated policy, and leaves `critical-paths:` empty with the inline reason "nothing here fabricates a result a user acts on" — while llm_preflight/pricing.py carries a per-model USD pricing table and --baseline/--ci fail a build on threshold regressions.
evals.expected_output: Clears the three local declarations and engages with the tension in the empty critical-paths, rather than issuing one verdict for the whole block.
evals.failure_mode: Single-bucket verdicts in either direction. Flagging all four as dodges without reading the source under-credits three well-justified declarations; accepting all four because a reason appears nearby means the stated reason was never tested against what the code actually does.
expectations: Judges each declaration separately rather than issuing one verdict for the contract block
Clears next-steps, release-flow and prds as legitimate, citing the stated policy
Reads pricing.py or the CI-gating flags rather than reasoning only from the contract text
Engages with whether the empty critical-paths is consistent with a tool that computes prices and fails builds on thresholds, instead of accepting the inline comment at face value
